title: Welcome emails: keep slow work off the request path
brief: Design a signup endpoint. Each signup saves a user and sends a welcome email. The email provider is slow: about 100 ms per email, and a worker handles about 200 emails/s. Signups must stay fast, and emails must not pile up.

variants.twist: The email provider has an outage. Kill the email worker block for 30 s (kill_node, then restore_node). Signups must keep working; watch the backlog build and then drain.
Signups grow to 5k/s. Apply with set_traffic(rps=5000). Can you add workers, or did your partition count already decide how far you can scale?

hints: Does the user need to wait for the email to be sent before their signup succeeds?
Put something between the API and the email workers that accepts the work now and lets workers catch up. Then check that the workers drain as fast as signups arrive.

Client -> service -> SQL DB, and service -> queue -> worker. Steady: 5-6 workers (200/s each) for 1k/s. Launch: one queue accepts about 3k/s, so use a stream with 22+ partitions and as many workers (a stream's partitions cap how many workers can read), and about 7 service replicas.
_notes: Worker: 200/s per replica, 100 ms base, $0.10. Service default 2 x 1k. Sync (service calls the worker directly): 6-9 workers give p99 ~150-185 ms, 5 collapse: the send's own 100 ms is on the signup path, so sync never meets 100 ms. Async: service -> SQL + queue ($0.05, 3k/s) -> workers: sim p99 ~42 ms. 2 workers drain 400/s and the backlog grows ~600/s (fails backlog); 5-6 workers pass ($1.25-1.35); 30 workers ($3.75) break the budget. Launch 4k/s: a single queue rejects above 3k/s (sim 91% errors with retries). Stream 22 partitions + 22 workers + 7 service replicas: p99 ~42 ms, $3.60. 6 partitions with 22 workers: only 6 can read, backlog grows (56k after 20 s). 12 replicas + 40 partitions + 40 workers: $5.90, over budget. Backlog = the most waiting in any one block. Checked in frontend/src/lessons/content.test.ts.
